outcome: Draft prototypes, dialogue variants, metadata and Arabic–English localisation faster from rights-cleared assets — with provenance recorded and human authorship preserved
overview: Content backlogs and localisation queues delay releases: quest variants, item descriptions, store metadata and Arabic voice and text all wait on the same small teams. This solution drafts variants and translations from rights-cleared assets, approved style guides and an agreed glossary, records provenance for every generated asset, and routes everything through named human creators who edit and approve before anything enters a build. Cultural and dialect review for Gulf audiences is a required step, not an option. A 6–10-week pilot on one asset set targets faster approved turnaround at agreed quality and terminology thresholds. Human authorship and IP ownership stay with the studio.

benefits.text: Reduce turnaround time on approved content and localisation work by around 30%
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Measured on approved output only — drafts that fail review do not count; gains depend on glossary and style-guide maturity and on reviewer availability

benefits.text: Record rights, provenance and the approving human for every released asset

benefits.limits: Provenance covers assets produced through the governed pipeline; assets introduced outside it are not tracked, and the customer owns rights clearance and talent contracts

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); source assets, glossaries and generated drafts remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs, under no-training contractual terms

notFor.situation: Asset and code rights are unclear or unlicensed
notFor.why: Generation from assets the studio cannot prove it may use transfers legal risk into the build; the allowlist has nothing safe to draw on

notFor.situation: No creative review capacity to edit and approve drafts
notFor.why: The design requires a named human creator to approve every released asset; without reviewers the pipeline produces unusable volume

notFor.situation: A brief to replace creative staff rather than support them
notFor.why: The solution is scoped as assistance under human authorship, and its quality claims depend on creator review; no headcount-replacement outcome is offered or measured

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns rights clearance, talent contracts, creative approval and authorship of every released asset · Duration: 6–10-week pilot; further 12–22 weeks to studio scale
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, generative-AI engineer, Arabic localisation specialist; customer creative director, narrative and art leads, localisation owner, legal and IP reviewer · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
